div.head: III Atr 3.1
div.ab: ⁊ þæt man habbe gemót on ælcum wæpenkace; ⁊ gán út þa yldestan XII þegnas ⁊ se gerefa mid, ⁊ swerian on þam haligdome, þe heom man on hand sylle, þæt hig nellan nǽnne sacleasan man forsecgean ne nænne sacne forhélan.

Et habeantur placita in singulis wapentakis; et exeant seniores duodecim taini et prepositus cum eis, et iurent super sanctuarium, quod eis dabitur in manus, cur neminem innocentem uelint accusare uel noxium concelare.

⁊ þæt man habbe gemót on ælcum wæpen[t]ace; ⁊ gán út þa yldestan XII þegnas ⁊ se gerefa mid ⁊ swerian on þam haligdome þe heom man on hand sylle, þæt hig nellan nǽnne sacleasan man forsecgean ne nænne sacne forhélan.

Und dass in jedem Wapentake Gericht gehalten werde; und es sollen die vornehmsten zwölf Thegnas hervortreten, und der Vogt mit, und auf die Reliquie, die man ihnen in die Hand giebt, schwören, dass sie keinen schuldlosen Mann [rügend] verklagen, noch einen schuldigen verhehlen werden;

And that a court be held in every wapentake; and let the twelve leading thegns go out, and the reeve with them, and swear on the relic which is given into their hands that they will not accuse any innocent man nor conceal any guilty one;

And a court shall be held in every wapentake, and the twelve leading thegns along with the reeve shall go out and swear on the relics which are given into their hands, that they will not accuse any innocent man or shield any guilty one.

And that a meeting is to be held in each wapentake, and the twelve leading thegns, and with them the reeve, are to come forward and swear on the relics which are put into their hands that they will accuse no innocent man nor conceal any guilty one.

Dieser Satz sollte neues Kapitel beginnen.—Nicht die Gerichtshaltung ist das Neue, sondern die Rügejury, so dass der erste Satz diese nur ins Gericht jeden Wapentakes zu verlegen dient

This sentence ought to begin a new chapter.—What is new is not the holding of the court but the jury of presentment, so that the first sentence serves only to place this jury in the court of each wapentake
Nicht ‘[an Jahren] älteste’; s. Wb: eald 6; vgl.: Siferð ⁊ Morcære þa yldestan [angesehensten] þegenas into Seofonburgum; Ann. Agsax. 1015
Not ‘oldest [in years]’; see Wb: eald 6; cf.: Siferð ⁊ Morcære þa yldestan [most eminent] þegenas into Seofonburgum; Ann. Agsax. 1015

Vgl. Gl Geschworene 1.a; Urteilfinder 6; Thegn 8d. Auch u. 12. 13, 3 scheint unter þegn nur Vollfreier verstanden.—In der Auslegung steh ich in Ggs. zu Brunner (Schwurger. 404), dem K. Maurer (Gesetzspre. in Dän. 391) gegen Steenstrup (Danelag 215) zustimmte. Eine Anglo-Dän. Jury sehen in III Atr auch Worsaae (Dänen in Engl. 106f.), Palgrave (Commonwealth I 213); Forsyth (Trial by jury 68); Marquardsen (Haft 51); Maurer (in Kr. Übsch. V 389); Pol Mai I 121; Maitland (Sel. pleas manor. I p. xxxvi). Brunner verbindet das Leumundzeugnis im folg. c. 4 hiermit. Dieses aber hängt, wie in der Vorlage I Atr, wo keine 12 Geschworene voraufgehen, nur mit der Ordalschwere (3, 4) zusammen; es wird vom Herrn abgegeben, u. z. von ihm allein, denn von dessen möglichem Ggsatz gegen die Meinung der 12 ist keine Rede.—Ich halte mit Steenstrup die 12 identisch mit den Urteilfindern u. 13, 2, und erblicke darin die nur weiter, wahrscheinlich in Nordischem Geiste, organisierte ‘Ältesten’-Kommission des Gerichtes; s. d. 20ff.—Eine ähnliche Institution sind die Lagamen; s. d. Gl

Cf. Gl Geschworene 1.a; Urteilfinder 6; Thegn 8d. Below, in 12. 13, 3 too, þegn seems to be understood as only a fully free man. — In my interpretation I take the opposite view to Brunner (Schwurger. 404), with whom K. Maurer (Gesetzspre. in Dän. 391) agreed, against Steenstrup (Danelag 215). An Anglo-Danish jury in III Atr is also seen by Worsaae (Dänen in Engl. 106f.), Palgrave (Commonwealth I 213); Forsyth (Trial by jury 68); Marquardsen (Haft 51); Maurer (in Kr. Übsch. V 389); Pol Mai I 121; Maitland (Sel. pleas manor. I p. xxxvi). Brunner connects the testimony to character in the following c. 4 with this. That testimony, however, is connected only with the severity of the ordeal (3, 4), as in the source I Atr, where no 12 jurors precede; it is given by the lord, and by him alone, for there is no mention of his possibly taking a view opposed to the opinion of the 12. — With Steenstrup I hold the 12 to be identical with the judgment-finders below 13, 2, and see in them the ‘elders’ committee of the court, merely organized further, probably in a Scandinavian spirit; see that word 20ff. — A similar institution is that of the lawmen; see that word in Gl

Das gán (s. d. Wb 2) dient nur das folgende Handeln (Schwören) einzuführen. Mit Unrecht versteht ‘inquirere’ Steenstrup (Danelag 210), gestützt auf: [Wilhelm I.] lett agan ut, hu fela hundred hyda wæron innon þære scire; Ann. Agsax. 1085. Earle und Plummer verstehen ‘herausbekommen, entdecken’, dagegen Toller (Suppl. 28b V): ‘sich ergeben, resultieren’. Aber gan ist nicht agan und, wenn St.'s Deutung zuträfe, würde das Objekt zu ‘erforschen’ hier fehlen

The gán (see that word in Wb 2) serves only to introduce the action that follows (swearing). Steenstrup (Danelag 210) wrongly takes it as ‘inquirere’, relying on: [William I] lett agan ut, hu fela hundred hyda wæron innon þære scire; Ann. Agsax. 1085. Earle and Plummer take it as ‘find out, discover’, whereas Toller (Suppl. 28b V) takes it as ‘turn out, result’. But gan is not agan, and if St.'s interpretation were correct, the object of ‘investigate’ would be missing here

‘schuldig sprechen’ (Hermann Schöffengericht 237 nach Phillipps) ist eine nicht belegte Bed. Auch wo Homilien forsecgan to deaðe brauchen (Ælfric ed. Thorpe I 50, II 208), reden sie nicht vom Richter oder Urteilfinder, sondern übersetzen Vulgatastellen von testes, die accusant

‘to pronounce guilty’ (Hermann Schöffengericht 237, following Phillipps) is an unattested meaning. Even where homilies use forsecgan to deaðe (Ælfric ed. Thorpe I 50, II 208), they are speaking not of the judge or the judgment-finder, but are translating Vulgate passages about testes who accusant
Ein Abstraktum sacen (Schmid 650), das auch Forsyth und Earle annehmen, gibt es nicht. Vielmehr liegt ein Nord. Adj. vor; s. Wb, auch unsac; Toller 806b. 808b
There is no abstract noun sacen (Schmid 650), such as Forsyth and Earle also assume. Rather, what we have is a Norse adjective; see Wb, also unsac; Toller 806b. 808b

Cf. II Edw. 2 and perhaps IV Edg. 5, but it is a question whether this council of 12 is not a Scandinavian institution connected, if not substantially identical with, the lawmen. Since from 13, 2 the twelve thegns evidently act as a jury they may be compared with the juries of 12 so frequently mentioned in sagas relating both to Norway and Iceland, e.g. Egilssaga, Ch. 56, where three such act in combination, Eyrbyggja saga, Ch. 16. In Gylfaginning, Ch. 14, the gods themselves are credited with a similar institution (cf. also Ynglinga saga, Ch. 2), and there can be no doubt that it was of high antiquity in the north. Its historical connection with the juries of later times is disputed.
Cf. Norse saklauss.
Cf. Norse sekr, accused, guilty (opp. unsac), and see BT. p. 806, s.v. sac, where no other instance of the use of this adj. is quoted.
